toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The problem is concentrated in one place. Eight of the 11 associates on the Kestrel matter resigned, against 1 of 13 elsewhere in the group. Other groups have normal attrition, so this is not general market mobility or the firm-wide hours target. Pay doesn't explain it either. Our associates sit at roughly the market median, the rival firm pays £3–5k more rather than the £15k quoted, and most leavers took equal or lower pay. A £12k retention payment would cost about £228k and aim at the wrong cause, so don't announce it or close the review.

What we can't yet say is whether the cause is the Kestrel workload or the supervision by Dorian Faulk. All 11 Kestrel associates were supervised by Faulk, and he supervises no one else, so the records can't separate the two. Survey comments point to both: weekend work, and late-night corrections copied to the whole team. I'm moderately sure about the concentration and fairly sure pay isn't the cause. I'm not sure which of workload or supervision matters more.

Next steps: commission the roughly £9k confidential external interviews, designed to separate workload from supervision, and get results before the document-review phase ends in December. Add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition reporting. Hold the £160k contract-review team and the supervision change until the interviews report, unless leavers keep going in the meantime.
